title: A manual run is started from a form that lists the jobs and their inputs
Generate the Manual workflow's form from the config (job dropdown, one field per input, validate and verify)
body:
Epic gcd-8f83, part 1 of 3 (planning doc `.pearls/docs/epics/gcd-8f83.md`, "What ships", first item). Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## Context (re-validated against the code on 2026-11-28)

The Manual workflow template `templates/workflows/manual.yml` is fixed text: `workflow_dispatch` (lines 74-85) asks for two free-text fields, `job` (type string) and `inputs` (a JSON object of strings). Its header comment says "Every generated file is fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block; this file does not vary with the config at all" (lines 13-15) and "The file cannot list a job's inputs, since it does not vary with the config" (lines 27-28). In `git-cicd`: `render_workflow(config, tool, template)` (line ~1011) replaces only `__SCHEDULE__\n` (built by `schedule_block(config)`, line ~1001, which writes each cron with `json.dumps`) and `__TOOL__`; `rendered_triggers`/`stale_paths`/`render_workflows`/`verify_workflow` (lines ~1024-1104) decide which files are generated and compare them whole. Inputs are validated by `_validate_inputs` (line ~211; `INPUT_NAME_RE = ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, `INPUT_FIELDS = description, required, default, choices`; description already single-line printable) and jobs by `_validate_job`/`validate_config` (lines ~332-520; normalized job has `manual` = `job.get("manual", True) is not False`).

The decision (agreed, do not reopen): the Manual workflow varies with the config, as the cron workflow's schedule block does. Only the Manual workflow changes; `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml` and `git-cicd-cron.yml` must stay byte-identical (their templates are not edited, including their header comments).

## Scope

1. `templates/workflows/manual.yml`: replace the fixed `inputs:` block under `workflow_dispatch` with a placeholder (e.g. `__FORM__`) that `render_workflow` fills from the config, the same way `__SCHEDULE__` is filled for cron. Update this template's header comment to state the new rule: the generated files are fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block and the Manual workflow's form; whoever changes a job's inputs or adds/removes a manual job runs `generate` and commits.
2. A `form_block(config)` (name free) that writes, in config order of `config["jobs"]`:
   - `job`: `type: choice`, `required: true`, `options:` the names of the jobs whose normalized `manual` is true, in config order, with a description. Job names are already validated identifiers (`JOB_NAME_RE`).
   - one field per distinct declared input name of those jobs, in first-seen order (config order of jobs, then declaration order of inputs). Each field carries the declaration's description, its default, and for an input with `choices` `type: choice` with `options:` the choices (a dropdown); otherwise `type: string`.
   - every generated input field is `required: false` in the form, since the form shows every job's fields at once; the tool keeps enforcing `required` for the chosen job (decision, see below).
   - when a field is not used by every manual job, its description says which jobs use it (e.g. `Version bump type (job release)`; exact wording free, but stable and tested).
   - every description, default and option is written with `json.dumps` (a JSON string is a valid YAML double-quoted scalar), exactly as `schedule_block` writes cron expressions. Input names are written bare (they match `INPUT_NAME_RE`).
3. Sharing: an input declared by more than one manual job under one name appears once. `validate` refuses (as a `ConfigError` line) declarations of one name that cannot share a field: different `choices` (including one with choices and one without) or different `default` (an absent default and `""` count as different only if the implementer documents it; decision: treat absent and `""` as the same, since both give the empty string to the script, see `input_values`). The message names the input and the jobs, and what to change (e.g. `input bump_type is declared by jobs release and other with different choices; give them the same choices and default, or rename one`). Differing descriptions are allowed: the field uses the first job's description (decision; descriptions do not change the value a script gets).
4. Reserved name: `validate` refuses an input named `job` on a job that allows manual runs (it would collide with the form's `job` field), naming the job.
5. Platform limit: GitHub allows at most 25 inputs in a `workflow_dispatch` workflow (GitHub changelog 2025-12-04 "Actions workflow_dispatch workflows now support 25 inputs"; was 10). Re-check the current limit in GitHub's documentation when implementing and put the source in a code comment next to the constant (e.g. `MANUAL_FORM_LIMIT = 25`). The `job` field counts, so at most 24 distinct input fields. `validate` refuses a config whose form would exceed it, with the count and the limit and what to change (fewer distinct input names, or `"manual": false` on a job).
6. No job allows a manual run: `generate` does not write `.github/workflows/git-cicd-manual.yml` (and removes it when present), and `verify` fails while it is still there, naming `generate` — the same treatment as the cron workflow when no job has cron (`rendered_triggers`, `stale_paths`, the "is still there" message in `verify_workflow`). Reason: a `choice` input needs at least one option, and a Manual workflow with nothing to run must not exist, mirroring cron. The `job` field's dropdown is never empty.
7. `verify` covers the form like the schedule block: since `verify_workflow` regenerates and compares whole files, adding or changing an input, adding a manual job or setting `"manual": false` without regenerating fails `verify` with the diff and `run: <tool> generate and commit ...`.
8. `templates/config.schema`: update the `jobs` description for inputs (named fields in the Manual workflow's form, shared by name across jobs, the `job` reserved name, the form limit). Leave the sentence about how values are given (`a manual run gives values as a JSON object in the Manual workflow's inputs field`) for gcd-8f83.2 to rewrite, or rewrite it here if this lands after it.

Out of scope here (other issues of this epic): how the tool reads the form's values on a run and the removal of the free-text `inputs` field and `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` (gcd-8f83.2; until then the template keeps the `inputs` free-text field as the last field and its env lines unchanged, so a run still works); hostile-declaration tests (gcd-8f83.2); regenerating this repo's own workflow, README and AGENTS.md (gcd-8f83.3). Not in scope: one workflow per job, `key=value` input, any change to `open`/`merge`/`cron`.

## Decisions recorded

- Fields are `required: false` in the form and required-ness stays enforced by the tool for the chosen job: a `required: true` field would force the owner to fill inputs of jobs they did not choose.
- Absent default and `""` are the same default for sharing: both give the script the empty string.
- Differing descriptions of a shared input do not refuse the config; the first job's description is used, plus the "used by" note.
- An input named `job` is refused for manual jobs (collides with the `job` field).
- Limit 25 including `job`; source in a code comment.
- No manual job: no Manual workflow file (mirrors cron), verify flags a stale one.

## Tests (pytest, following `tests/test_workflow.py` and `tests/test_config.py` patterns)

- The form for a config with two manual jobs and one `"manual": false` job: `job` options list exactly the manual jobs in config order; each input appears once, with description, default, and `type: choice` + `options` for choices; the "used by" note appears only on fields not used by every manual job. Parse the generated file with a small YAML-subset check or exact-text comparison (no new dependency; standard library only).
- A shared input with identical declarations appears once; differing choices and differing defaults are each refused with a message naming the input and both jobs.
- An input named `job` on a manual job is refused; on a `"manual": false` job it is allowed.
- 24 distinct inputs pass; 25 are refused with `25` and the limit in the message.
- No manual job: `generate` writes no manual file and removes an existing one; `verify` fails while it exists and names `generate`.
- `verify` fails after an input is added or changed without `generate`, naming the command, and passes after `generate`.
- `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml`, `git-cicd-cron.yml` rendered for a config are byte-identical to what the current templates give (a test pinning that `render_workflow` of those templates is unaffected by inputs/manual flags).
- Coverage of `git-cicd` stays at 99% or more (`./git-cicd check --job test`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `./git-cicd generate` writes a Manual workflow whose `job` is a dropdown of the manual jobs in config order and whose other fields are the declared inputs, once each, with description, default and, for choices, a dropdown.
- `validate` refuses incompatible shared declarations, an input named `job` on a manual job and a form over the platform limit, each naming what to change.
- With no manual job no Manual workflow is generated, and `verify` fails while a stale one exists.
- `verify` fails when the form and the config disagree, naming `generate`.
- Open, Merge and Cron workflows are byte-identical to before.
- `./git-cicd check` passes with coverage at 99% or more; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing (no vendor-protected file touched).

title: Read manual inputs from the form's named fields only; remove the free-text inputs field; hostile-declaration tests
body:
Epic gcd-8f83, part 2 of 3 (planning doc `.pearls/docs/epics/gcd-8f83.md`, "What ships", second item). Depends on gcd-8f83.1 (the form generated from the config). Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## Context (re-validated against the code on 2026-11-28)

Today the Manual workflow (`templates/workflows/manual.yml`) has a free-text `inputs` field (lines 81-85) passed as `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS: ${{ inputs.inputs }}` to the decide step (line 148) and the run step (line 190). In `git-cicd`: `MANUAL_INPUTS_ENV = "CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS"` (line ~75), `parse_manual_inputs(text)` (line ~277, JSON object of strings), `input_values(job, given)` (line ~294: refuses an undeclared key, a value outside choices, a missing required input when `given` is not None; else default, else `""`), `manual_input_values(job)` (line ~324), used by `decide_manual` (line ~634, via `manual_refusal` at line ~618) and `run_job` (line ~902, manual branch at ~910-916, which raises `UsageError("manual run refused: ...")`). `script_env` (line ~861) sets one `CICD_INPUT_<NAME>` per declared input and strips inherited `CICD_INPUT_` variables and `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS`. Injection rules (README "No accidental injection"): form values reach the tool and scripts only as environment variables, never on a command line and never as `${{ }}` inside a `run:` block.

## Scope

1. Remove the free-text `inputs` field from the Manual workflow's form and `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` from the tool. The decide and run steps instead set one fixed env line, `CICD_MANUAL_FORM: ${{ toJSON(inputs) }}` (name free, but one variable; decision below), so the env blocks stay fixed text and no form value appears in a `run:` block. The tool reads manual values on one path only: a replacement for `parse_manual_inputs`/`manual_input_values` that reads `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` (a JSON object of strings from the form; the `job` key is ignored, since the job comes from `--job`), then gives the chosen job's declared inputs to `input_values`. `MANUAL_INPUTS_ENV`, `parse_manual_inputs` and their tests go; `script_env` strips `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` instead of `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS`.
2. A run passes only the fields of the chosen job to it. A field the chosen job does not declare is ignored, not an error, since the form shows every job's fields: when its value differs from the field's form default (the declared default; else the first choice for a dropdown, which GitHub preselects; else `""`) the decision records it and the report says so (e.g. `ignored input vendor (job release does not declare it)`); a field left at its default is ignored silently. `decide_manual` and `run_job` agree (the same function).
3. Required inputs: an empty value from the form for a required input of the chosen job counts as missing, and the run is refused with `job <name>: input <key> is required` (the form cannot mark it required, see gcd-8f83.1). A value outside its choices is still refused. Refusals keep today's shape: decide records the reason, needs no job, the report is FAILED with it; `run-job` exits 2.
4. Locally (`decide --trigger manual`, `run-job --trigger manual`) the same variable is read; without it every input is its default (required inputs refused).
5. Hostile declarations: names written into the generated file are validated identifiers (`JOB_NAME_RE`, `INPUT_NAME_RE`); descriptions, defaults and choice values are written with `json.dumps` (gcd-8f83.1). Add `validate` refusal of `${{` in a description, default or choice of a job that allows manual runs, naming the job and input — decision: GitHub evaluates `${{ }}` in workflow strings and YAML has no escape for it, so refusing is the only way to guarantee it is not evaluated. Defaults and choices with a newline are written escaped by `json.dumps` (`\n`) and stay one line.
6. Update the Manual template's header comment (lines 21-33) for the new event and reading path.

## Tests (pytest in `tests/test_workflow.py`, `tests/test_decide.py`, `tests/test_run.py`, `tests/test_config.py`)

- Hostile-declaration test: generate from a config whose descriptions, defaults and choices contain `'`, `"`, `:`, `#`, `$`, backticks, `\n` (defaults/choices), `{{` and leading/trailing spaces; show the file is still one well-formed workflow (the `workflow_dispatch.inputs` keys are exactly the expected names, each value round-trips with `json.loads` of the written scalar) and that no `run:` block in any generated file (open, merge, cron, manual) contains any value taken from the config. `${{` in each of description/default/choice is refused by `validate`.
- `decide --trigger manual` and `run-job --trigger manual` with `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` set: the chosen job gets its inputs as `CICD_INPUT_<NAME>` (a step script prints its env); a value with quotes, `$`, backticks and a newline reaches the script literally.
- A non-default value for a field of another job is ignored and reported; a default one is ignored silently.
- Missing/empty required input, value outside choices, malformed `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` (not JSON, not an object of strings) are refused with the reason in the report.
- `CICD_MANUAL_FORM` and inherited `CICD_INPUT_*` do not reach scripts.
- The template has no `inputs` free-text field and no `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS`.
- Coverage of `git-cicd` stays at 99% or more.

## Decisions recorded

- One env variable `CICD_MANUAL_FORM: ${{ toJSON(inputs) }}` rather than one env line per field: keeps the step env blocks fixed text (only the form varies), one reading path, values only in an env var.
- Ignored fields are reported only when they differ from the field's form default; otherwise every run would report every other job's prefilled defaults.
- An empty value for a required input is missing.
- `${{` refused in manual jobs' descriptions, defaults and choices.

## Acceptance criteria

- The Manual form has no free-text `inputs` field; the tool has one path for reading manual values.
- A manual run with fields set gives the chosen job its inputs as `CICD_INPUT_<NAME>`, shown by tests for `decide` and `run-job` on the manual trigger; values reach a script literally.
- Undeclared fields are ignored and reported when non-default; refusals (required, choices, malformed) still report the reason.
- Hostile-declaration tests pass; no `run:` block in any generated file contains a value taken from the config.
- `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml`, `git-cicd-cron.yml` byte-identical to before the epic.
- `./git-cicd check` passes with coverage at 99% or more; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: Regenerate git-cicd's own Manual form and document the form in README and AGENTS.md
body:
Epic gcd-8f83, part 3 of 3 (planning doc `.pearls/docs/epics/gcd-8f83.md`, "What ships", third item). Depends on gcd-8f83.1 and gcd-8f83.2. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## Context (re-validated against the code on 2026-11-28)

`.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` (editable vendor config, not vendor-protected) declares `test` (open), `release` (merge on main; inputs `bump_type` choices patch/minor/major default patch, `subdirectory` default "", `changelog_description` default ""), `vendor-check` (open) and `update-vendored` (cron `0 9 * * 1` on main; inputs `vendor` default all, `version` default latest, `private` choices true/false default false). No job sets `manual`, so all four allow manual runs today (`manual` defaults to true).

## Scope

1. Config: set `"manual": false` on `test` and `vendor-check` in `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json`, so the form's `job` dropdown is exactly `release` and `update-vendored` as the epic's acceptance criteria require. Decision: AGENTS.md says the owner starts only `release` and `update-vendored` by hand; the open jobs run on pull requests.
2. Run `./git-cicd generate` and commit `.github/workflows/git-cicd-manual.yml`. It must have a `job` dropdown with `release` and `update-vendored` and the named fields `bump_type` (dropdown patch, minor, major; default patch), `subdirectory`, `changelog_description`, `vendor` (default all), `version` (default latest) and `private` (dropdown true, false; default false), each with its description and default, and a note of the job using it (none is shared). `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml`, `git-cicd-cron.yml` unchanged byte for byte.
3. `tests/test_own_jobs.py`: assert the generated form for this repo's config (the job options and the six fields with descriptions, defaults and choices).
4. `README.md`:
   - "The generated workflows" (line ~384; the manual bullets at ~460-480 now describe two free-text fields, `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` and `-f inputs='{"bump_type": "minor"}'`): state the changed rule — the generated files are fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block and the Manual workflow's form (which jobs are listed, which fields, how shared names and the limit work); show the form an adopter gets (an example `workflow_dispatch` block); `gh workflow run git-cicd-manual.yml --ref main -f job=release -f bump_type=minor`; no Manual workflow when no job allows manual runs.
   - "The config" / "Declared inputs" (lines ~101-157; "Giving values" at ~138-143 and "Failures" at ~148-157 describe the JSON `inputs` field): rewrite for named fields, shared names, the `job` reserved name, `${{` refusal, the form limit (25 including `job`), ignored fields reported, required enforced by the tool.
   - Say that changing a job's inputs, adding a manual job or changing `manual` means `generate` and a commit in the same pull request (verify fails otherwise).
   - An upgrade note for adopters coming from a version with the two free-text fields: regenerate and commit; `-f inputs=...` and `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` no longer exist; jobs that should not appear in the dropdown set `"manual": false`; anything scripting `gh workflow run ... -f inputs=` switches to one `-f <name>=<value>` per input.
   - "Developing git-cicd" (line ~690; the manual-run text at ~700-707 with `{"bump_type": "minor"}`): how the owner starts `release` or `update-vendored` by hand now (pick the job, fill the named fields); `test` and `vendor-check` are not manual.
   - Check the "Commands" table (line ~674) and "No accidental injection" (line ~229) for anything mentioning the JSON field.
5. `AGENTS.md` ("This repository's jobs" and "Vendored tools"): replace "the `inputs` field as JSON (for example `{"bump_type": "minor"}` or `{"vendor": "mangimangi/git-semver"}`; empty for the defaults)" with the named fields (job `release` with `bump_type` etc., job `update-vendored` with `vendor` etc.), and mention that a change to a job's inputs regenerates the Manual workflow.
6. Template header comments: only `templates/workflows/manual.yml` (done in gcd-8f83.1 and gcd-8f83.2; check it matches the README). The comments of `open.yml`, `merge.yml` and `cron.yml` ("Every generated file is fixed text except the cron workflow's schedule block", line 13) are NOT changed, because those generated files must stay byte-identical (decision; the README carries the rule).

No vendor-protected file is added, changed or deleted; `.vendored/install` is not run.

## Acceptance criteria

- The committed `.github/workflows/git-cicd-manual.yml` matches `./git-cicd generate` and has the `job` dropdown `release`, `update-vendored` and the fields `bump_type` (patch, minor, major), `subdirectory`, `changelog_description`, `vendor`, `version`, `private`, each with its description and default; `./git-cicd verify` passes.
- `git-cicd-open.yml`, `git-cicd-merge.yml`, `git-cicd-cron.yml` byte-identical to before the epic.
- README states the changed rule, shows the form, says inputs changes need `generate` and a commit, and has the upgrade note; AGENTS.md says how a job is started by hand here; no doc mentions the JSON `inputs` field or `CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS` except the upgrade note.
- `./git-cicd check` passes with coverage at 99% or more; the pull request into `plan/git-dev-883c` has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.
